description: Joseph J. Avery — Introducing the “Hard” Problem of Artificial Legal Intelligence (NYU L. Rev. Online 2026)
show_notes:
Joseph J. Avery — Introducing the “Hard” Problem of Artificial Legal Intelligence (NYU L. Rev. Online 2026)

Avery argues that AI-drafted judicial opinions and statutes raise a “hard” problem distinct from the familiar “easy” ones of accuracy, transparency, and accountability: whether law produced or substantively shaped by artificial systems can keep the normative legitimacy of human-made law, even if it replicates human legal reasoning perfectly. He groups the main arguments for that problem — law’s essentially deliberative character, its reliance on first-person moral judgment, and empirical evidence that people see machine-authored law as less authoritative. He then proposes treating “Artificial Legal Intelligence” as its own field of legal scholarship.
